Not applicable here regardless of the rule's readiness elsewhere.

consequence: If the component unmounts (user navigates away) while the awaited async work (clipboard copy, OAuth switch/logout fetch, diagnostics collection) is still pending, the callback resumes after await and calls `.set()` on reactive state whose effect still writes to now-detached DOM nodes. This is at minimum a wasted write to disposed state and, if the effect's cleanup already ran, a null/stale-reference write; the exact bug class the sibling PRs' tests (`ignores a continuation load that resolves after ... removed`, `stops writing ... once its boundary is detached`) were added specifically to catch and prevent.

existing_plugin_coverage: No published ESLint rule covers this: it depends on recognizing this repo's specific `reactive.js` state/effect/createFactoryScope convention and its abort-signal idiom, not a generic async/await or React-hooks pattern that an existing plugin (eslint-plugin-react-hooks, eslint-plugin-promise, etc.) targets.
likely_false_positives: An async handler that calls `.set()` after `await` but whose component is never removed from the DOM during that async work (e.g. a top-level page-scoped singleton that outlives all navigation) does not need the guard; the rule should only fire when the enclosing scope is created via `createFactoryScope()`/bound to a removable node, i.e. an abort signal is already available in scope but unused after an await preceding a `.set()` call.
mechanical_correction: After every `await` inside an async handler that subsequently calls `state.set(...)`, check `if (scope.signal.aborted) return;` (or the component's equivalent abort signal) before performing the write, mirroring the guard already present in #15419, #15463, and #15483.
syntactic_constructs: async () => { ... await ...; ...State.set(...); } inside an onClick/observer callback
createFactoryScope() + state() + effect({ signal: scope.signal }) component shape (reactive.js, factory-elements.js)
missing `if (scope.signal.aborted) return;` directly after an awaited call and before a subsequent `.set()`
unsafe_pattern: An async event handler (button onClick, IntersectionObserver callback, etc.) that is refactored from direct DOM mutation into a `state()` value written from an `effect()`, but the post-await `.set(...)` calls inside the async callback are not guarded by the component's `createFactoryScope().signal.aborted` check before writing. Two of five near-identical refactors merged in this window ( #15434 account-menu, #15475 configuration-view) omitted the guard that the other three (#15419 ui-primitives, #15463 table-region, #15483 data-view) added for the same busy/status-state extraction.
